[TODAY] A spacecraft flying rectangles around an asteroid. ☄️

ESA's Hera spacecraft, about the size of a small car, has reached Didymos, an asteroid about 780 m across, and its 151 m moon Dimorphos. That is the moon NASA's DART spacecraft crashed into on purpose in 2022, shortening its orbit by about 33 minutes.

Gravity there is so weak (up to 200,000 times weaker than Earth's) that Hera flies a slow, steered path instead of a normal orbit. It drifts at about 12 cm per second and fires its thrusters every 3 to 4 days, turning 90 degrees each time: a rectangle in space. Next it moves closer, about 20 km away, on bowtie-shaped paths.

Reality check: whether DART left a crater or reshaped the whole asteroid is still unknown. Finding out is Hera's job.

[TODAY] Robotaxis just started rolling in Munich. 🚕

Today, Nov 18, Uber and the self-driving company Momenta opened a robotaxi pilot across large parts of northern Munich, including the area around the Olympic Park. Riders can join an interest list in the Uber app. Selected riders who book an UberX, Electric or Comfort trip in the zone may be offered an autonomous ride, with pick-up and drop-off at set stops.

The rides are free during the pilot, which runs under a test permit from Germany's Federal Motor Transport Authority. The plan is to grow step by step toward a regular service.

Reality check: a trained safety operator is on board every ride, and the fleet size hasn't been shared.
